{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZkuqrg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDLTPU", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 95, "title": "Implement NTSC non-interlaced long-dot and short-scanline timing", "body": "## Problem

The NTSC scheduler treats every scanline as 1,364 master clocks, and horizontal counter capture assumes four clocks per dot. There is no field-parity state. This leaves long-dot counter conversion, the alternating-field short scanline, and STAT78 field reporting unimplemented.

At baseline `028ec9f4e519a865e9f3e5f8e28728a7eb4e6224`:

- [`SystemBus::tick`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/028ec9f4e519a865e9f3e5f8e28728a7eb4e6224/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L190) rolls every line at the fixed `LINE` constant and every frame after 262 lines.
- [`bus_tick`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/028ec9f4e519a865e9f3e5f8e28728a7eb4e6224/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L502) also uses that fixed line boundary when splitting accesses around refresh.
- [`Ppu::latch_counters`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/028ec9f4e519a865e9f3e5f8e28728a7eb4e6224/crates/snes-core/src/ppu.rs#L290) captures `h / 4`; STAT78 never supplies field bit 7.

Correcting this geometry is a prerequisite for more accurate counter access, interrupt scheduling, controller polling, and eventual raster behavior. This Issue implements geometry and counter conversion; it does not complete those broader features.

## Expected outcome

Implement NTSC non-interlaced timing with SETINI interlace and overscan disabled, including during forced blank.

### Hardware contract and evidence prerequisite

Reconcile the following contract against [Fullsnes, Timing H/V Counters, Timing H/V Events, and STAT78](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm) and [SNESdev Timing](https://snes.nesdev.org/wiki/Timing). These references are attributed by the repository's [Issue #35 record](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/docs/issue-35-validation.md) and [Issue #5 record](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/docs/issue-5-validation.md).

The planner inspected only repository content. The referenced specification snapshots are absent locally, so the exact external wording and field-number conventions were not independently rechecked. Before coding, record the source revisions/sections and resolve any disagreement. If authoritative evidence contradicts a numeric requirement below, document and correct that requirement before freezing the tests; satisfying an unsupported draft requirement is insufficient.

The contract to confirm and implement is:

- Horizontal counter values run from 0 through 339. On ordinary lines, dots 323 and 327 each last six master clocks; other dots last four. The line totals 1,364 clocks.
- In the non-interlaced field reported by STAT78 bit 7 as 1, scanline V=240 lasts 1,360 clocks: both normally long dots last four clocks. Other lines retain ordinary geometry.
- Each field contains 262 scanlines. The ordinary and shortened fields total 357,368 and 357,364 clocks respectively; a pair totals 714,732 clocks.
- Field parity changes at field rollover and is exposed through STAT78. Preserve its existing latch acknowledgement, read-selector reset, version, NTSC region, and open-bus behavior.
- SLHV and WRIO-triggered captures convert the current master-clock position using the active line geometry. Preserve their existing gate, held-value, and independent read-selector semantics.
- Initial/reset parity must be documented as an emulator convention unless supported by physical reset evidence. With initial parity 0, the first field is ordinary and the second contains the short line.

Useful independent counter anchors, expressed as half-open master-clock intervals from line start:

| Line | H=323 | H=327 | H=339 | Rollover |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ordinary | [1292,1298) | [1310,1316) | [1360,1364) | 1364 |
| Short | [1292,1296) | [1308,1312) | [1356,1360) | 1360 |

### Focused implementation scope

Use consistent active-line geometry in scheduler advancement, refresh/access splitting, and PPU counter capture. Advance the APU by actual elapsed master clocks without resetting its phase at raster boundaries.

Retain existing whole-line rendering and early horizontal event conventions. HBlank at 1096 clocks and HDMA eligibility at 1112 precede the long dots; this Issue supplies no evidence to move them. The four-clocks-per-dot wording in the Issue #35 record must be qualified rather than extended into a universal counter formula.

Re-derive automatic joypad opportunities from corrected field boundaries while preserving the existing 256-clock lattice and documented 4,224-clock duration. Update only directly dependent browser pacing and audio-duration expectations: use the confirmed two-field cadence, with independent parity-aware clock accounting in the regression oracle.

Non-goals: interlace, overscan, PAL, pixel-fetch rendering, DMA startup/alignment, refresh-revision phase differences, electrical latch strobes, warm-reset retention, and full IRQ assertion/sampling accuracy. In particular, PPU dot conversion does not establish the CPU timer comparator's delay or late-HTIME behavior; the existing `HTIME * 4` comparison remains a separately documented limitation.

## Context and reproduction

The latest assessment identifies this scheduler work as the next prerequisite. The supplied history contains no corresponding completed improvement or open Issue. Issue #93 expanded BRR evidence without changing runtime hardware behavior.

Existing rollover tests in `machine.rs` calculate expectations using `LINE` and fixed frame multiplication, so they cannot independently establish variable geometry.

One assessment detail needs correction: [`joypad_auto_tests.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/028ec9f4e519a865e9f3e5f8e28728a7eb4e6224/crates/snes-core/src/machine/joypad_auto_tests.rs#L326) explicitly uses a 357,368-clock fixed raster. Its separate `NEXT = START + 357376` represents an aligned polling interval, not the frame duration. Recalculate polling opportunities across alternating fields; do not blindly replace every occurrence of 357,376.

The browser also assumes fixed geometry in [`web/app.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/app.js#L10) and [`cleared-games.spec.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/tests/cleared-games.spec.js#L129).

Planning was read-only. No tests were executed and no files were changed.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record the specification reconciliation before implementation: dot numbering/durations, short-line V coordinate and field-bit relationship, field rollover, and the distinction between beam geometry and IRQ assertion delays. Separate source statements, arithmetic deductions, and emulator conventions.
- [ ] Implement the confirmed runtime behavior. Add original Rust regressions with literal expectations independent of production timing constants/helpers. Cover every clock around both long dots, H=339 and rollover, ordinary versus short V=240, adjacent V=239/241, both parities, and at least four naturally advanced fields. Assert line totals, field totals, cumulative clocks, and STAT78 parity.
- [ ] Exercise SLHV and WRIO captures through timed bus accesses on both geometries. Preserve gate behavior, held counters, independent selectors, STAT78 acknowledgement, and open-bus assertions. Demonstrate behavioral failures of new geometry/counter tests on the exact baseline, rather than compilation failures.
- [ ] Add an original source-built 65C816 guest that reaches both field parities through ordinary execution, records counter/field observations in WRAM, and terminates with an asserted result and bounded deadline. Do not inject beam, parity, IRQ, or result state from the host. Record authorship, license, construction, and expected-value derivations in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`.
- [ ] Verify one-clock, irregular, and whole-interval advancement across multiple fields produces identical observable timing state. Check timed CPU accesses and DMA crossing the short-line boundary; refresh must occur once per line, with no lost access clocks. Verify existing IRQ/NMI events are neither lost nor duplicated at corrected rollovers, explicitly retaining their unresolved physical offsets.
- [ ] Re-derive joypad lattice expectations across alternating fields and a lattice wrap. Retain all existing serial, interference, busy, completion, and reset controls. Update directly dependent browser cadence/audio equations without increasing drift tolerances.
- [ ] Preserve existing game source pins, hashes, inputs, frame counts, progression checks, audio checks, and negative controls. Correct timing-only expectations solely with explicit specification evidence; do not regenerate expected gameplay results merely to obtain a pass.
- [ ] Run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --workspace --locked`. Include the new tests in normal workspace execution. Preserve the existing counter-latch, joypad, refresh/interrupt, DMA/HDMA, PPU-port, and APU timing regressions.
- [ ] Run the existing source-built hardware gates documented in [README Validate](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/README.md#validate): reproducible smoke fixture; pinned tool builds; `tools/hardware-tests.py` with the documented ca65, ld65, and spcasm paths; and `tools/ppu-test.py` with the documented bass path. Use only original or explicitly licensed, pinned source-built fixtures.
- [ ] Run the existing browser gate after repeated cleared-game source builds and a fresh Wasm/web build: `npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'`, following README dependency setup. This must retain mandatory cleared Castle/Memory gameplay, progression, audio, queue/drift, reset, and persistence checks. No commercial ROM or firmware acquisition is required.
- [ ] Record commands, actual results, baseline counterexamples, and remaining limitations in a validation record. Passing these bounded checks must not be described as full hardware accuracy or commercial compatibility.

Remaining scheduler work includes precise IRQ/NMI comparator/assertion/sampling offsets, revision-dependent refresh/startup alignment, complete device synchronization, interlaced/overscan geometry, and physical fetch/arbitration timing.

Retain all 24 inventory scopes without narrowing them: `cpu`, `bus`, `scheduler`, `dma`, `hdma`, `controllers`, `ppu-bg`, `ppu-offset`, `ppu-hires`, `ppu-mode7`, `ppu-objects`, `ppu-color`, `ppu-ports`, `ppu-display`, `spc`, `ipl`, `dsp-voices`, `dsp-noise`, `dsp-pitch`, `dsp-envelope`, `dsp-echo`, and `dsp-timing` remain partial; `ppu-raster` and `pal` remain unimplemented. None becomes fully verified through this Issue.

## Optional validation

Physical-device traces of the bounded timing cases, if already available with explicit provenance. They are not required for merge.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
